;Disasters and accidents
*[[2019 Iran floods]]
**The [[Iran]]ian government announces an emergency in southwestern provinces threatened by flooding and worked to evacuate dozens of villages as forecasters predicted more of the [[March 2019 North Iran Floods|heavy rains]] that have killed at least 45 people last week. [https://www.reuters.com/article/us-iran-floods/iran-calls-emergency-in-flood-threatened-southwest-province-idUSKCN1RB0F3 (Reuters)]
*The death toll from thunderstorms in southern [[Nepal]] rises to 30. Several houses are ruptured, trees uprooted and vehicles overturned in [[Bara district]] and [[Parsa district]]. [https://www.bbc.com/news/world-asia-47772482 (BBC News)]
*Thirty firefighters die in southwestern [[China]] after a forest fire trapped them due to a sudden shift in winds. [https://www.nytimes.com/2019/04/01/world/asia/china-fire-sichuan.html (''The New York Times'')] [https://www.bbc.com/news/world-asia-china-47772483 (BBC)]
*Two children are killed and twenty are injured in [[China]] after a [[dust devil]] lifts an [[inflatable castle]] off the ground. [https://www.scmp.com/news/china/society/article/3004174/two-children-killed-when-bouncy-castle-swept-air-dust-devil (''South China Morning Post'')]

;Health and environment
*[[China]] announces that it will add [[fentanyl]] to a list of regulated narcotic drugs on May 1, 2019, in an effort to curtail its manufacturing. [https://www.bbc.com/news/world-asia-china-47772484 (BBC News)] [https://www.cnn.com/2019/04/01/asia/china-us-fentanyl-trump-intl/index.html (CNN)] [http://time.com/5561887/china-regulate-fentanyl-drugs/ (''Time'')]
*Aftermath of [[Cyclone Idai]]
**The first death due to [[cholera]] is confirmed in [[Mozambique]], with confirmed cases rising to 517. [https://www.cbsnews.com/news/cholera-outbreak-cyclone-mozambique-first-death-disease-spreads-fast/ (CBS News)] [https://www.independent.co.uk/news/world/africa/cyclone-idai-mozambique-cholera-death-beira-a8848971.html (''The Independent'')]

;Politics and elections
*[[2019 Turkish local elections]], [[Erdoğanism]]
**In an election [[2019 Turkish local elections#Controversies|marred by electoral fraud]], [[Turkey]]'s ruling [[Justice and Development Party (Turkey)|Justice and Development Party]] wins with 44% of the vote while [[Republican People's Party (Turkey)|Republican People's Party]] comes in second with 30% of the vote. Overall, [[People's Alliance (Turkey)|People's Alliance]] gets 51% of the vote while [[Nation Alliance (Turkey)|Nation Alliance]] receives 37% of the vote. [[Voter turnout]] was 84%. [http://secim.aa.com.tr/#en (Anadolu Agency)]
*[[2019 Japanese imperial transition]]
**{{Nihongo|[[Reiwa period|Reiwa]]|令和}} is revealed as the new [[Japanese era name|Japanese Era name]] set to start on May 1 upon [[Crown Prince Naruhito]]'s [[Enthronement of the Japanese Emperor|accession]] to the [[Chrysanthemum Throne]] as the 126th [[Emperor of Japan]]. [https://www.japantimes.co.jp/news/2019/04/01/national/politics-diplomacy/japan-readies-announce-name-new-era/ (''The Japan Times'')]
*[[2019 Guatemalan general election]]
**The [[Supreme Electoral Tribunal (Guatemala)|Supreme Electoral Tribunal]] accepts the nullity recourses against the candidacy of [[Thelma Aldana]] and temporarily leaves her out of the general elections. However, an appeal will be filed before the Supreme Court of Justice and ultimately, the [[Constitutional Court of Guatemala|Constitutional Court]]. All three top candidates face serious legal challenges that may prevent them from running. [https://www.prensalibre.com/guatemala/politica/tse-rechaza-inscripcion-de-thelma-aldana/ (''Prensa Libre'')] [https://www.foxnews.com/world/guatemala-election-court-puts-former-prosecutor-out-of-race (Fox News)] [https://www.aljazeera.com/amp/news/2019/04/guatemala-top-presidential-contenders-face-expulsion-race-190402151350957.html (Al Jazeera)]

*[[2019 Algerian protests]]
**[[President of Algeria|Algerian President]] [[Abdelaziz Bouteflika]] announces that he will resign by April 28, following intense pressure from the military and the ruling party to step down amid anti-government protests, bringing an end to his 20-year rule. [https://www.reuters.com/article/us-algeria-protests-businessmen/algerias-bouteflika-to-resign-before-mandate-ends-april-28-state-media-idUSKCN1RD217 (Reuters)]
*[[Brexit negotiations]]
**The [[Parliament of the United Kingdom|British parliament]] votes against four alternative [[Brexit]] plans. [https://www.cbc.ca/news/world/brexit-monday-indicative-votes-1.5079353 (CBC)]
**Protesters strip naked in the public galleries of the [[House of Commons (United Kingdom)|House of Commons]], pressing their buttocks against the window facing Ministers. [https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=OVdl6lKxG-Q (''The Guardian'' via YouTube)] [https://www.theguardian.com/world/2019/apr/01/semi-naked-climate-protesters-disrupt-brexit-debate (''The Guardian'')]
*[[Michele Muratori]] and [[Nicola Selva]] are sworn in as [[Captains Regent of San Marino|Captains Regent]] of [[San Marino]]. [https://www.corriereromagna.it/news/san-marino/34819/ambiente-sociale-economia-e-turismo-il-programma-dei-capitani-reggenti-a-san-marino.html (''Corriere Romagna'')]
